12a. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request Standing Committee on Urban Technologies, Innovation and Environment review testimony provided to the Committee at its December 15, 2025, meeting by Councilor Etel Haxhiaj related to the city’s Social Media Policy failing to address concerns relative to posts made by members of the Worcester Police Department (WPD) on their Police Union Facebook page.
12b. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request Standing Committee on Municipal and Legislative Operations hold a public hearing relative to receiving feedback as to ways the city’s social media policy can be updated and/or more properly enforced.
12c. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON VETERANS' MEMORIALS, PARKS AND RECREATION - Request Standing Committee on Veterans’ Memorials, Parks and Recreation invite representatives from Friends of Newton Hill and the Newton Square Neighborhood, South Lenox Street Neighborhood, and Saxon Road Neighborhood Groups to a public forum for the purpose of demonstrating to said groups a presentation relative to the planned improvements to Newton Square in Elm Park and to promote community engagement with the project.
12d. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC SAFETY - Request City Manager request Police Chief provide City Council with a report detailing the turnover rate of the Worcester Police Department’s (WPD) officers, including any reasons why officers are leaving the department. Further, request said report include best practices relative to increasing the number of police officers and retaining officers currently employed by WPD.
12e. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager request Chief Information Officer and City Solicitor provide City Council with a report concerning technology available to monitor the social media usage of the city’s employees on city-owned devices. Said report should include an assessment as to why such technology would or would not infringe upon an employee’s First Amendment right to freedom of speech.
12f. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager provide City Council with a report concerning whether the Worcester Police Department (WPD) has a different social media policy than the rest of the city. Further, request said report include information concerning the feasibility of including within any WPD social media policy a code of conduct that addresses the behavior of WPD employees online towards both public officials and any residents or citizens in the city. Further, request said report also include a list of all WPD social media pages.
12g. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager provide City Council with a report concerning any efforts made by the city to address concerns brought forth by the public and elected officials over posts made by city employees on their social media accounts.
12h. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager provide City Council with a report concerning the process used by the city’s various department to make a press release.
12i. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager provide City Council with a report concerning the feasibility of updating the city’s Social Media Policy.
12j. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager request Chief Information Officer provide City Council with a report concerning best practices used in other communities relative to monitoring the social media usage of its employees, including specific technology used for such a purpose.
12k. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager request Chief Sustainability Officer provide City Council with seasonal updates relative to data associated with the water bodies in the city.
12l. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager provide City Council with a report of the Lake Quinsigamond Commission minutes from 2025.
12m. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON URBAN TECHNOLOGIES, INNOVATION AND ENVIRONMENT - Request City Manager provide City Council with a quarterly scorecard detailing the status of the Department of Sustainability and Resilience’s various priority action items. Further, request the first such scorecard be provided in the first quarter of 2026.
12n. FROM THE COMMITTEE ON VETERANS' MEMORIALS, PARKS AND RECREATION - Request City Manager consider allocating funds for the Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) to complete the improvements to Newton Square in Elm Park.
13. ORDERS
13a. Request City Manager provide City Council with a report concerning the proliferation of traffic-calming seasonal and permanent speed humps on residential streets throughout the city. While these speed humps improve the safety of people who walk, bike, and play in neighborhoods, said report should detail the parameters used to approve and place speed humps in appropriate locations and what warning signage is needed as motorists approach these raised structures. (Rosen)
13b. Request Standing Committee on Public Service and Transportation hold public hearings, and later make recommendations, encouraging the Worcester Regional Transit Authority (WRTA) to improve bus service to the city’s residents and businesses. Potential considerations for improvements should include, but not be limited to, the implementation of rapid transit, route changes, a same day paratransit pilot program, improved service times, and a review of the desirability of their hub and spoke operations. Participants invited to said hearings should include, but not be limited to, local bus transit riders, the WRTA Administrator and the Chairman of their advisory Board, representatives from the Zero Fare Worcester Coalition, the local Riders Action Council, faculty and students in the Department of Urban and Environmental Policy and Planning at Tufts University, the city’s Department of Transportation and Mobility, the city's Commission on Accessibility, the Worcester Department of Public Health, the statewide Transportation for Massachusetts (T4MA) agency and MassDOT. (Rosen, Bilotta)
13c. Request City Manager require Spectrum to finally fulfill its contractual obligation to provide, even retroactively, all senior subscribers in Worcester to its cable TV service, with a long-overdue senior discount. (Rosen)
13d. Request City Manager provide City Council with a report relative to the status of the city’s 911Application/Alert Worcester, the City’s Automated Emergency Notification System 911 Emergency Alert System (Worcester 911), including information relative to whether the city is in the process of identifying a new vendor for such a purpose. Further, request said report also include information concerning the usage plans for such a system moving forward, including how residents will be effectively notified of winter parking bans, severe weather alerts, community weather alerts, notices from DPW parking bans, trash pickup delays, street closures etc. Further, request City Manager grant relief to any residents who received tickets during winter parking bans due to lack of notification by the city, including texts and phone calls. (King, Rivera, Bilotta, Bergman)
13e. Request City Manager request Commissioner of Public Works provide City Council with a report detailing the feasibility of expanding the spring street sweeping program to include the pickup of leaves and branches that were not picked up during the fall program. (Rivera)
13f. Due to extensive community concern and to ensure the safety of motorists, pedestrians and preteen to adult bicyclists alike, request City Manager request the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and all the city's traffic, mobility and enforcement experts review and provide City Council with a report, long before construction begins, concerning the Massachusetts Department of Transportation's current design and plans to make pedestrian and bicycle improvements to Pleasant St. (Route 122) from Tatnuck Square to the Paxton line. The state's proposed plan involves reconstructing existing sidewalks, constructing new 5-foot-wide sidewalks where feasible, and adding 5-foot-wide bike lanes along the roadway. Acquisitions in fee and permanent or temporary easements may be required. And there are unanswered questions regarding whose responsibility it will be to shovel snow from these sidewalks. While MassDOT has the right to make decisions in state highway matters, the city of Worcester, the city’s residents and business owners have the responsibility to speak up and to act if there are legitimate safety concerns with this or any other road project. (Rosen)
13g. That the City Council of the City of Worcester does hereby amend its meeting schedule to cancel its March 3, 2026, City Council agenda and make the March 10, 2026, City Council meeting a joint City Council and City Manager agenda, to accommodate the Jewish holiday, Purim. (Petty)
13h. Request City Manager provide City Council with a draft ordinance similar to the ordinance passed in the City of Boston (see attached) requiring retail pharmacies in the city to establish a collection system (such as an indoor or outdoor kiosk) and to accept hypodermic needles, lancets, and other sharps from the public at no charge for proper disposal. (Rosen)
13i. Request City Manager request Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility identify and prioritize pedestrian improvement projects along the Lake Ave. corridor, as identified in the Vision Zero priority network. Said pedestrian improvement projects should include curb extensions, raised crosswalks/intersections, high visibility crosswalks, rapid flashing beacons, pedestrian hybrid beacons, enhanced pedestrian lighting and pedestrian refuge islands/raised medians. (Bilotta)
13j. Request City Manager request Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility identify and prioritize pedestrian improvement projects on Lincoln St., between Brittan Square and Interstate 290. Said pedestrian improvement projects should include curb extensions, raised crosswalks/intersections, high visibility crosswalks, rapid flashing beacons, pedestrian hybrid beacons and enhanced pedestrian lighting. (Bilotta)
13k. Request City Manager provide City Council with a report concerning if and to what extent the Department of Public Works collaborates with the Worcester Public Schools during winter weather events to aid in determining the appropriateness of delaying the opening of schools and/or granting a full snow day. (King)
13l. Request Standing Committee on Traffic and Parking hold a meeting to discuss best practices the city can use to guarantee traffic signage is finalized by City Council and installed in all proper locations in a timely and efficient manner, to better ensure safe and properly enforceable signage is installed throughout the roadways of the city. (Rivera)
13m. Request City Manager request Commissioner of Public Works require all contractors have all detour and road closure signage up and visible, with a list of businesses that are still open to the public also clearly marked, whenever road construction of any kind shuts down a street or a section of street with businesses located inside the location. (Economou)
13n. Request City Manager request Chief Development Officer consider ensuring an ombudsperson be available to all small business owners for the purpose of helping them through the city’s permitting process, in an effort to expedite and remove confusion around what is required from a business relative to permitting, building out their infrastructure, and all other processes required prior to opening and/or renovating their businesses. (Economou)
13o. Request City Manager request Chief Development Officer and Commissioner of Inspectional Services work together to determine ways to simplify and eliminate any unnecessary requirements around permitting in the city. Said effort should include ensuring applicants recognize the difference between when a request is made of them as opposed to when something is required of them prior to any applications they have pending before the various board and commissions can be approved. (Economou)
13p. Request City Manager work with the Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility and Police Chief to provide City Council with a report detailing the effectiveness of the statutory city-wide speed limit of 25 miles per hour. Said report should include information concerning the feasibility of enforcing said program and whether any additional resources or devices are required to effectively monitor said speed limit, including whether additional law enforcement officers would be required to properly enforce such a speed limit. (Mitra)
13q. Request City Manager request Commissioner of Transportation and Mobility provide City Council with a report examining best practices used in other communities relative to their resident permit parking programs. Said examination should include information concerning how other communities work with students attending college in their city to ensure they can park in the areas they live, as well as the appropriateness and feasibility of instituting “zoned” resident parking in the city, which may allow for residents to request multiple streets in a small area to have portions of their street reserved for resident permit parking and allow for increased ability to enforce the regulation. (Rivera)
13r. Request City Manager request Police Chief provide increased speed and traffic enforcement on Lake Ave. from Bigelow Davis Parkway/Hamilton St. to Sunderland Rd. (Fresolo)
13s. Request City Manager request Chief Development Officer provide City Council with a report outlining CSX’s Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) agreement with the city, including information concerning CSX’s compliance with all aspects of said agreement, including but not limited to their compliance, or lack thereof, with trucks operating and driving in the Grafton Hill area causing traffic concerns in the neighborhood. (Fresolo)
13t.
